seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through August, when Bachelor Creek and Itswoot Ridge are passable and the glacier approach still has bridged crevasses

June.reason: Deep snow on Itswoot Ridge and the Cub Lake basin, avalanche-loaded slopes, and high snowmelt creeks make the multi-day Downey Creek approach impractical.

July.reason: Snow still covers much of the upper approach, which eases the glacier travel, but early in the month cornices and wet slides remain a hazard.

August.reason: The off-trail approach is mostly melted out, glacier bridges are still usable early on, and the granite on the east face is dry and warm.

September.reason: The glacier approach is bare and more crevassed, days are much shorter for a one-to-two-day approach, and the first fall storms can arrive.

October.reason: Early snow on the high approach, freezing cracks and very short days leave little margin on this remote, loose route.

evidence: Row approach/hazards: Downey Creek TH off Suiattle River Road, southern Ptarmigan Traverse via Itswoot Ridge/Cub Lake/Bachelor Creek, glacier travel
